pairs.why: B matches the real light's muted navy body, grey metal truss and practical build; A's yellow bumpers and chunky rounded parts make it read as a toy.
A keeps the real chair's all-green fabric and grey tubes with a cleaner folding frame; B's orange armrests and puffy curved back move away from the reference.
A's thicker star with soft volume and a faceted gem is closer to the chunky, saturated finish of the real items; B is thinner, with harder metallic edges.
B's rope is smoother and has softer shading, like the real cards, and its coil-and-loop build reads clearly; A's heavy twist texture is the too-texture-y look the lessons marked down.
A keeps the reference's simple layout (target on an easel, teddy, light-bulb frame, red backdrop); B adds extra props and a brick wall, which crowds the card.
A's bottle has a believable shape, a slim loop and a slightly translucent finish closer to the real bottle; B is a squat, opaque, glossy toy shape.
B sets the train in a full painted scene with believable proportions, like the bus and bike cards; A is a rounder toy locomotive on a bare backdrop.
B's chunky posts, smooth wood and simpler water are closer to the real dock; A's water has busy, realistic caustic texture.
